# WhimsyDesk

> Free, open source desktop organizer apps for Mac: real-feeling objects (a fridge, a wooden drawer, a post box and two vending machines) that sit on your desktop and hold your files. Files are moved into normal folders, never copied or deleted, and Put Back returns each file to its exact desktop spot. No accounts, no tracking. macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. The fridge also has a beta for Windows 10 and 11.

Made by Krrish Parmar, a product designer in Mumbai (https://krisby.in). MIT licensed. Source: https://github.com/Electrofist/WhimsyDesk

## Objects

- [Desktop Fridge](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-fridge/): a retro fridge with a heavy swinging door, cold fog, frost on files left too long, sticky notes and photo magnets. Stores files in ~/Fridge.
- [Desktop Drawer](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-drawer/): a wooden drawer that slides up from the bottom of the screen, with friction, bumpers and wooden sounds. Stores files in ~/Desktop Drawer.
- [Desktop Mailbox](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-mailbox/): a red post box where handpicked letters arrive now and then, including short real letters from history; also hides files behind its door. Stores files in ~/Mailbox.
- [Desktop Vending Machine](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-vending-machine/): files stand on shelves; press a button and one drops into the tray.
- [Desktop Vending Machine Keypad](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-vending-machine-keypad/): the same machine with a keypad; type a code like B2 to drop a file.
- [Desktop Fridge for Windows](https://whimsydesk.art/desktop-fridge-windows/): beta for Windows 10 and 11, with an installer.

## Guides

- [How to clean up your Mac desktop without losing files](https://whimsydesk.art/clean-up-mac-desktop/)
- [Fun things to put on your Mac desktop](https://whimsydesk.art/fun-mac-desktop/)
- [Make your own desktop object](https://whimsydesk.art/make-your-own/): a template where you draw two pictures and set where files go. No Swift needed.
- [FAQ](https://whimsydesk.art/faq/)

## Notes

- Downloads are free DMGs from GitHub releases. The apps are not notarized by Apple yet, so the first launch needs System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway.
- Nothing commercial: no paywalls, ads or in-app purchases.
